positive_controls.description: RE-SCOPED (authority amendment S2-1): a verification record for the provisioned principal asserts the BRANCH-AWARE property set LIFECYCLE.phases[1].must_prove yields after MGP-PD2 is resolved for the actual subject -- one positive (a session can be obtained) and, depending on that resolution: (a) TRIGGER_ABSENT/TRIGGER_INAPPLICABLE -- the original five negatives (no profile row, no membership, no database role or grant, no organization-scoped surface reachable, no production-project credential); or (b) TRIGGER_ACTIVE -- the NARROWER four negatives that survive a trigger-created row (is_super_admin false on it, no membership, no database role or grant, no organization-scoped surface reachable, no production-project credential), with the absent-row claim explicitly marked INAPPLICABLE_WITH_TRIGGER_ACTIVE rather than attempted or silently dropped. A verification record missing the MGP-PD2 resolution that decides which branch applies is REJECTED as incomplete, matching PC-P7's own procedural requirement -- this control and PC-P7 are companions, not duplicates: PC-P7 proves the resolution HAPPENS, PC-P5 proves the RIGHT property set is asserted once it has.

negative_controls.description: RE-SCOPED (authority amendment S2-2/S2-3): the principal cannot reach any organization-scoped surface: a request carrying its session to a tenant-scoped route is refused. Proves PD-3 (no organization membership) produces real containment on its own, UNCONDITIONALLY -- exercised with MGP-PD2 in BOTH resolutions (a fixture where the trigger is simulated active and a fixture where it is simulated absent), asserting the refusal holds identically in either case. Where PD-2 ALSO holds (no profile row), the control additionally asserts there is no row to have granted a narrower single-tenant surface either; where PD-2 does not hold, the control asserts containment rests on PD-3 and PD-4 alone and does not depend on the absent-row claim.

RE-SCOPED (authority amendment MANIFEST_CONSUMER_PROPAGATION.NC-P6_and_the_fourth_reason_code): a 302 from Deployment Protection, a 429 from the global rate limiter, and a transport error -- the THREE ORIGINAL reason codes -- are each recorded as INCONCLUSIVE with a distinct reason code, and are never collapsed into PASS or FAIL (M11-SC-6). Each of these three is exercised, not just asserted in prose. The fourth reason code, IDENTITY_PROVIDER_INTENTIONALLY_UNAVAILABLE, is NOT covered by this control -- see NC-P12.

RE-SCOPED (authority amendment S2-1/B1_TRIGGER_ANALYSIS): the observation path never invokes the application's login, signup, onboarding or OAuth-callback flows. Asserted structurally against the four measured syncUserProfile call sites, because traversing any of them would perform an ADDITIONAL profile write beyond whatever the database-plane trigger does, on the first run, with no error raised. This control proves the APPLICATION-layer discipline holds; it does NOT by itself prove PD-2, which additionally depends on MGP-PD2's hosted-trigger resolution (PC-P7). A test asserting this control passing therefore may NOT be read, on its own, as proof that no public.users row was created.

FOURTH INCONCLUSIVE REASON CODE (authority amendment QUIESCE_INCONCLUSIVE_REASON): a sign-in attempt failing while a governed QUIESCE or recovery posture has intentionally made GoTrue unreachable is recorded INCONCLUSIVE with reason code IDENTITY_PROVIDER_INTENTIONALLY_UNAVAILABLE, and is NEVER collapsed into FAIL. FUTURE-DEPENDENT: exercising this control requires a capability to ask whether a quiesce posture is CURRENTLY declared for the project, which QUIESCE_INCONCLUSIVE_REASON.open_dependency records as unspecified here. Until that capability exists, this control's positive exercise is STATUS=FUTURE_MATERIALIZATION with an unresolved dependency, distinct from the other three reason codes' FUTURE_MATERIALIZATION (which depends only on the runner existing); an offline/unit-level exercise against a SIMULATED quiesce-declared response is permitted and does not require the dependency to be resolved first.
